title: An accept refused for a dirty tree leaves the node open, not done
name: accept-dirty-done
description: Seen on 2026-09-24 with sync-branch-dx8l. In `packages/core/src/review.ts`, the direct-merge path calls `acceptNode(...)`, which writes `accepted` and makes the node done, before `mergeNode(...)` in `packages/core/src/merge.ts`. `mergeNode` then refuses an unclean checkout (`the working tree has uncommitted changes — accept would merge into them`, merge.ts:33). The tool returns that error, but the node is already done and its work never landed. `review` then says "already done, nothing to accept", so the only way out was a hand merge. The comment above `acceptNode` names exactly this state ("a done node whose work never landed") as the one the order exists to prevent, but it guards only the pull-request path. Fix: on the direct path, merge first and write `accepted` only after `mergeNode` returns. Or run `mergeNode`'s refusals (dirty tree, and a non-clean merge via `git merge-tree`) before `acceptNode`. Either way a refused accept leaves no `accepted` record. accept-merge-state-mzvt covers the conflicting-merge case through the same ordering. Whichever lands first should fix the ordering once for both. Test: with a modified tracked file in the main checkout, `acceptWork` rejects, the node's record has no `accepted`, and development's HEAD is unchanged.
